transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

I guess I’m here because… I’ve been having a hard time leaving things alone at home. I keep going back to check the outlets and the locks, and sometimes tools or dust, like I need to fix it or make sure it’s right. It takes up a lot of my day, honestly, and I end up worn out… but I still don’t really feel sure enough to stop.
Do you find that you have certain thoughts or worries that come into your mind, even if you don’t want them, that make you feel like you have to check or fix things?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I know it probably sounds a bit much, and I don’t want to make it seem like I’m being dramatic, but even when I’m pretty sure I did something right, I get these thoughts that just jump in.

Like… what if there’s a loose wire I missed and the house burns down, or what if I left a nail somewhere and my wife gets hurt. I try to tell myself it’s fine and push it away, but then it comes back even stronger, and I feel like I have to go check or fix it again. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find yourself doing certain things over and over again, like checking, counting, or repeating actions in a specific way, even if you don’t really want to?

Yes… yeah, I do. I mean, I don’t really like admitting how much, but I spend a lot of the day going back over the same things — outlets, locks, my tools, even dust around the house — checking or fixing them again and again.

I’ll tell myself, “Okay, that’s enough,” but then I still don’t feel sure, so I go back. By the end I’m worn out, and it still doesn’t feel settled. Is that… is that what you’re asking about?
How much time do you estimate you spend each day checking or fixing things like outlets, locks, or dust?

Um… it’s probably more than I’d like to admit. I try to tell myself it’s just a few checks here and there, but honestly it ends up being most of the day.

I keep going back over the same outlets, locks, tools, and even dust around the house, checking or fixing them again and again. By the time I stop, I’m worn out, and I still don’t really feel sure enough to leave it alone.
Do these checking or fixing behaviors cause you a lot of stress or get in the way of other things you need or want to do during the day?

Yeah… I guess it does, more than I’d like it to. I don’t want it to sound like I’m just making excuses, but the house kind of ends up taking over my whole day.

I used to take paid carpentry jobs, and I helped with community projects sometimes, but I’ve pulled back from that because I get stuck checking and fixing things at home. My wife has had to handle more of the errands and decisions too, because I’ll still be there going over things, and by the time I’m done I’m just exhausted.

I know that probably isn’t great. Is that the kind of thing you mean by getting in the way?
Are these thoughts that come into your mind something you actively try not to have, and do they cause you a lot of anxiety or discomfort when they occur?

Yeah… I do try not to have them. I mean, I know I’ve usually done the job right, so I tell myself it’s fine and I shouldn’t think like that.

But then these thoughts just kind of jump in — like maybe I missed a loose wire and the house could burn down, or maybe I left a nail somewhere and my wife could get hurt. I don’t want to think those things. They feel… ugly, I guess. And the more I try to push them away, the louder they seem to get.

It does make me anxious, yes. I’m not trying to be dramatic, but it’s hard to just let it go when those thoughts come back. Is that what you mean?
Do you find yourself doing things in a very specific way or order, or performing certain actions repeatedly, even if they’re not directly related to checking outlets, locks, or dust?

I guess… yes, in a way. It’s mostly the same things I mentioned — the outlets, locks, tools, and dust — but I don’t just look once and move on like I probably should.

I’ll go back over them again and again, kind of in a set way, trying to make it feel finished or right. I’ll think, okay, just one more pass and then I can leave it alone, but then I still don’t feel settled, so I start over or fix something again.

I know it probably sounds excessive. I’m not trying to waste the whole day, but that’s what ends up happening, and by the end I’m just worn out and still not really sure I can stop.
Have you ever had thoughts, images, or urges that come into your mind that you find disturbing or unwanted, even when you’re not checking things like outlets or locks?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, not all the time, or at least I try not to let it be all the time.

But even when I know I did the work right, these thoughts kind of jump in anyway — like maybe there’s a loose wire I missed and the house could burn down, or maybe I left a nail somewhere and my wife could get hurt. I don’t want those thoughts. They feel really ugly, and I try to push them out, but then they come back even stronger.

I don’t know if that’s exactly what you’re asking, but… yes, they’re definitely unwanted.
When you check things like the outlets, locks, or tools, is it mainly because you feel you have to in order to prevent something bad from happening, like a fire or an accident?

Yes… I think that’s probably fair to say.

I try to tell myself I’m just being careful, you know, not careless. But honestly, I end up spending most of the day going back over the same outlets, locks, tools, even dust or little things around the house, checking and fixing them again and again.

It’s like I’m trying to get to a point where I feel sure enough that nothing bad will happen, but I don’t really get there. I just get worn out and still feel like I shouldn’t leave it alone. Does that make sense?
